questions.question: What property clips element overflow to border radius?
questions.explanation: overflow: hidden clips content to rounded borders.

questions.question: What CSS feature defines reusable values?
questions.explanation: CSS variables use --name syntax for reuse.

questions.question: What rule imports external CSS files?
questions.explanation: @import loads external stylesheets.

questions.question: What property controls flex item growth?
questions.explanation: flex-grow defines expansion proportion.

questions.question: What property controls flex item shrinking?
questions.explanation: flex-shrink defines reduction proportion.

questions.question: What property defines grid template areas?
questions.explanation: grid-template-areas names grid regions.

questions.question: What pseudo-element creates content before elements?
questions.explanation: ::before inserts content before elements.

questions.question: What pseudo-element creates content after elements?
questions.explanation: ::after inserts content after elements.

questions.question: What property creates complex animations?
questions.explanation: @keyframes defines multi-step animations.

questions.question: What property applies multiple background images?
questions.explanation: background-image accepts comma-separated values.

questions.question: What does the selector p::first-letter target?
questions.answer: the first letter of each paragraph
questions.explanation: ::first-letter styles only the initial letter of a block.

questions.question: Which selector wins a conflict: #nav or .nav?
questions.explanation: ID selectors have higher specificity than class selectors.

questions.question: Unlike visibility: hidden, what does display: none do to layout?
questions.explanation: display: none removes the element's space entirely.

questions.question: If .a { color: red } and .b { color: blue } both apply to one element, what color wins?
questions.explanation: With equal specificity, the last declared rule wins.

questions.question: What CSS function computes values like calc(100% - 50px)?
questions.explanation: calc() performs mathematical calculations in CSS values.

questions.question: A designer writes `.card { container-type: inline-size; }` and `@container (min-width: 400px) { ... }` so the card restyles itself from its parent's width rather than the viewport. What CSS feature is being used?
questions.explanation: Container queries let components respond to their containing element's size instead of the viewport.

questions.question: A site header must stay pinned to the top of the viewport only while its parent section is on screen, then scroll away naturally. Which position value achieves this?
questions.explanation: position: sticky acts relative until a scroll threshold, then fixes within its nearest scrolling ancestor.

questions.question: In `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr))`, which function constrains each track to a 200px minimum while letting it grow?
questions.explanation: minmax(min, max) bounds a track's size between a floor and a ceiling value.

questions.question: A developer writes `form:has(input:invalid) { border-color: red }` to style a parent based on its children. What is :has() formally classified as?
questions.explanation: :has() is the relational pseudo-class, matching an element relative to anchor elements inside it.

questions.question: A developer wants to recolor only the bullet of each <li> without touching the list text. Which pseudo-element targets list markers?
questions.explanation: ::marker selects the marker box of list items, allowing independent styling of bullets or numbers.
